newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares gain on finance minister's assurance.
newsitem.headline: India shares gain on finance minister's assurance.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) - India stocks record smart gains, mood firm
** Benchmark Bombay share index rallies 77.50 pts, or 2.7
pct to 2,958.65, off 2,966.99 intra-day high
** Indian finance minister's statement on Sunday that a
controversial new tax on companies may be phased out
enthuses marketmen
** Players build positions in blue-chips at start of new
settlement, local fund-UTI buyer in index-linked stocks
** National bourse index up 2.7 pct, Delhi index 2.3 pct,
Madras index 1.8 pct and the Calcutta index 1.22 pct

Indian bourses started the week on a buoyant note in hectic trade on Monday following an assurance by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram that a controversial new corporate tax might soon be phased out, dealers said.
"It was mainly the Chidambaram factor driving up the market," said a dealer at a domestic brokerage.
Chidambaram had said on Sunday that a controversial minimum tax on companies may be phased out after a new Income Tax Act and Companies Act came into force.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index surged 77.50 points, or 2.7 percent, to close at 2,958.65.

"The introduction of MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax) in the last budget has caused a high degree of discomfort to industry. It was introduced as a number of companies were paying dividend but not tax," Chidambaram told a seminar in Bombay.
The new tax introduced in July was aimed at high-growth firms that avoided paying taxes by ploughing back profits into new projects or expansions.
"MAT will definitely not go away, but there might be a simplification," said Ulhas Paymaster, a BSE broker.
Dealers said the MAT news gave a boost to market sentiment with speculators building positions in pivotals.
The Unit Trust of India, the country's biggest mutual fund was a major buyer in index-linked stocks, helping them stage a sharp rally, the dealers added.

ACC gained 89.50 rupees to 1,100, TELCO 17.50 to 335.50, Bajaj Auto 30.20 to 770.25, TISCO 5.25 to 158.75, Gujarat Ambuja 6.25 to 239.25, SBI 9.75 to 218.50, Nestle 15.0 to 195.0, Reliance 6.75 to 194.50 and MTNL 6.75 to 227.50. The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index rose 22.65 points to 847.27.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
